views.markdown:
Know the moment someone checks your location.

Chusma New Gen notifies you instantly whenever someone looks up your location through Apple's **Find My** — whether it's a device lookup (Find My Devices) or a person tracking you via location sharing (Find My People). Every lookup is saved to a full tracking log with timestamps.

**Jailbreak required.** Chusma hooks the Find My daemons, which needs tweak injection — it cannot run under TrollStore. The companion app alone is also offered as a `.tipa` for people who prefer installing it through TrollStore, but it only does anything alongside the tweak.

- **Instant alerts** the moment your location is requested
- **Real iOS notifications** via the bundled Chusma companion app — lock screen, Notification Center, the works
- **Notification sender** — or style the built-in banner with any app's icon (Tips, Maps, Clock, Calendar, Notes, Music, Mail)
- **Sound picker** with live preview
- **Custom message** text
- **Full tracking log** — every lookup with date and time, grouped by day
- **Statistics** — total lookups, today's count, last event
- **CSV export** of your complete history
- **Configurable cooldown** — 10s / 30s / 60s / 2m
- **Swipe to delete** entries or clear all

- **Remote lookups are detected again.** Three detection hooks were attached to classes that never implemented their selector, so they silently did nothing. The class names had been inferred from strings in the binary rather than checked against the running daemon. Scanned the live runtime and retargeted them:
  - receivedLocationCommand: is on SPSecureLocationsManager
  - _handleLocateIntent: and _handleSecureLocationsPush: are on FMDServiceProvider
  - _startLocateCycle... is on FMDLocationTracker
- **Detection now defaults to Strict**, which catches genuine remote lookups but ignores your own phone publishing its location when you open Find My
- Confirmed on-device: a lookup from another device reports via “locate command” and “secure-locations push”

- **Detection works again.** `killall` silently failed on the Find My daemons — it reported success while they kept running, so every upgrade left them on a stale dylib. Since 3.1.0 changed how the daemons and SpringBoard talk, that meant the two halves spoke different protocols and nothing was reported. The installer now uses `launchctl kickstart`, which actually cycles them
- SpringBoard also understands the pre-3.1 signals now, so a stale daemon can never silence detection again
- **Fixed Settings crashing** when opening the Chusma panel
- **Companion app is found when installed via TrollStore** — it lives under a random container UUID, so detection now asks LaunchServices instead of checking fixed paths
- Notifications post through BulletinBoard: SpringBoard has no UserNotifications entitlement to post for another bundle, so that route always failed
- Fixed stutter in the tracking log (the row icon was being redrawn for every cell on every frame) and glitching in Settings

- **The companion app is now its own package.** Shipping it inside the tweak meant a package manager owned the `com.fwbebo.chusma` bundle ID, so TrollStore refused to install the `.tipa` over it. Upgrading frees that ID
- **Signed the app with an `application-identifier` entitlement.** usernotificationsd keys authorization off it — without one the app showed the permission prompt but had nowhere to store the answer, which is why Allow came back denied and the app never appeared under Settings › Notifications
- Install the app from Sileo *or* via TrollStore, not both

- **Detection sensitivity** (Strict / Balanced / Everything) — Apple's Find My network republishes your location on a schedule to keep the device findable offline, and that background traffic was being reported as lookups. You can now filter those paths out
- **Hourly alert limit** (default 6) and longer cooldowns up to 1 hour
- **Separate Devices and People toggles**
- Filtered events are still logged — limits only stop the interruption
- **Fixed wrong Devices/People labels.** Someone in your People list usually reads the location your device already published rather than requesting a fresh one, and that path serves both tabs — so it now reports "Find My" instead of wrongly claiming "Devices"
- The Tracking Log now names the exact detection path behind every entry

- **Fixed a crash that sent SpringBoard to safe mode** when selecting the Chusma App sender. Notifications now go through UserNotifications instead of poking BBServer directly, which is thread-safe and reports failure rather than crashing
- Delivery failure now falls back to the built-in banner, so an alert always shows
- Fixed the app not updating its status after you tap Allow
- The app now detects when iOS accepts a grant but doesn't save it, and says how to fix it

- **Companion app added** — grants Chusma a real notification section, so alerts now appear as genuine iOS notifications on the lock screen and in Notification Center
- New "Chusma App" notification sender option
- Also shipping the app standalone as a `.tipa` for TrollStore
- Removed the Apple-app impersonation path: iOS 15+ silently drops bulletins for sections it doesn't own, so those choices now style Chusma's own banner with the app icon instead of failing quietly

- Sound picker with preview (Shake, Photo Shutter, Tink, Alarm, etc.)
- Notification sender selection — use any app's icon for the alert banner
- Custom alert message text
- Show Tracking Type toggle
- Modernized tracking log with inset grouped cards and colored icons

- Fixed detection not working on iOS 17 Dopamine — daemons are now restarted on install so hooks load
- Added iOS 17 Secure Locations hooks (FMDSecureLocationMonitor) for reliable detection
- Added rootless package scheme for Dopamine compatibility
- Architecture changed to iphoneos-arm64

- Fixed Find My app crashing on open (removed injection into Find My entirely)
- Chusma no longer loads into any app — only into the Find My daemons and SpringBoard
- Settings remain in the iOS Settings app as before

- Fixed crash in findmydeviced on iOS 17 that caused Find My to freeze and show stale locations
- Location replies now always go out before Chusma runs any detection code

- Added a Send Test Notification button — preview a real alert on demand from Settings
- Added Share Debug Log for easy troubleshooting without SSH
- Reorganized Settings for clarity

- Fixed notifications not appearing on iOS 17 (restored BulletinBoard display path)
- Added iOS 17 Find My People daemon (findmylocated)
- Added on-device debug logging

- Full rewrite for iOS 14–17
- Persistent tracking log with timestamps and daily counts
- Native log viewer with date grouping and swipe-to-delete
- CSV export, statistics, haptics, configurable cooldown
- Rootless jailbreak support (Dopamine / palera1n)
